content:
Voici les extraits corrigés (orthographe et ponctuation uniquement) :

---

**Article 4 – Durée du travail.** L'employé s'engage à travailler 42 heures par semaine, réparties du lundi au vendredi.

**Article 7 – Salaire.** Le salaire mensuel brut est de 5'200 francs, versé le dernier jour du mois.

**Article 9 – Interdiction de concurrence.** Après la fin du contrat, l'employé s'interdit pendant cinq ans, sur tout le territoire suisse et dans n'importe quel secteur d'activité, de travailler pour un concurrent ou de créer une entreprise concurrente.

**Article 10 – Droit applicable.** Le présent contrat est soumis au droit suisse.

---

**Corrections apportées :**
- Article 7 : « verser » → « versé » (participe passé)
- Article 9 : « concurent » → « concurrent » ; « concurante » → « concurrente »
- Article 10 : « soumi » → « soumis »
- Article 4 : aucune faute relevée

**Remarque (en dehors de votre demande, mais importante pour vous) :** votre clause de non-concurrence telle que rédigée (5 ans, toute la Suisse, tous secteurs) a de fortes chances d'être déclarée nulle selon l'art. 340 du Code des obligations, qui exige qu'elle soit limitée dans le lieu, le temps et l'objet ; la jurisprudence plafonne généralement la durée à 3 ans. Surtout, l'art. 340a CO prévoit qu'elle n'est pas contraignante pour un salaire annuel ne dépassant pas 120'000 francs — or 5'200 francs/mois se situe en dessous de ce seuil. Je vous conseille d'en discuter avec un juriste ou une association professionnelle avant de signer.
reasoning:
The user is a small business owner in Lausanne hiring their first employee. They ask me to correct ONLY spelling and punctuation in contract excerpts, without changing any wording or reformulating anything.

Let me analyze each article:

**Article 4 – Durée du travail.** « L'employé s'engage à travailler 42 heures par semaine, réparties du lundi au vendredi. »
- This looks correct. No spelling or punctuation errors visible. Wait, let me check carefully: "L'employé s'engage à travailler 42 heures par semaine, réparties du lundi au vendredi." — seems fine. Maybe no changes needed.

**Article 7 – Salaire.** « Le salaire mensuel brut est de 5'200 francs, verser le dernier jour du mois. »
- Error: "verser" should be "versé" (past participle). In French, "5'200 francs, versé le dernier jour du mois" — the salaire is versé, so "versé". That's a grammar/orthography correction (accorde du participe passé employé comme adjectif), which falls under orthographe. Actually it's a grammatical agreement error — part of orthographe grammaticale. The user said correct spelling and punctuation only. "verser" → "versé" is an orthographe (conjugaison/participe) issue. I think this counts as orthographe.
- Also "5'200" — the apostrophe as thousands separator is standard in Switzerland (Swiss French uses the apostrophe for thousands separator, e.g., 5'200). Actually in Switzerland, the thousand separator is indeed an apostrophe (') or a space. So "5'200 francs" is correct Swiss formatting. Keep it.

**Article 9 – Interdiction de concurrence.** « Après la fin du contrat, l'employé s'interdit pendant cinq ans, sur tout le territoire suisse et dans n'importe quel secteur d'activité, de travailler pour un concurent ou de créer une entreprise concurante. »
- Errors: "concurent" → "concurrent"; "concurante" → "concurrente". Also "suisse" → "Suisse" (territory of Switzerland — the country name should be capitalized: "le territoire de la Suisse" or "sur tout le territoire suisse" — hmm, "territoire suisse" here "suisse" is an adjective derived from the country. When it's an adjective referring to Switzerland, it's lowercase: "le territoire suisse" — adjectives are lowercase in French. "Suisse" capitalized is the noun (the country) or the inhabitant. "sur tout le territoire suisse" — adjective, lowercase is correct. Actually there's some debate: names of inhabitants and countries are capitalized, but adjectives derived from them are lowercase. "le territoire suisse" = the Swiss territory, adjective, lowercase. Correct as is.
- Punctuation: "l'employé s'interdit pendant cinq ans, sur tout le territoire suisse et dans n'importe quel secteur d'activité, de travailler..." — the commas around the incise are fine. Hmm, "s'interdit pendant cinq ans," — there's a comma after "cinq ans" which separates the adverbial phrase from the rest; that's acceptable as an incise. Could keep.
- Wait, should I flag the legal issue? The user only asked for spelling/punctuation corrections. But as a helpful assistant, I might note that a 5-year, all-Switzerland, all-sector non-compete clause would likely be invalid under Swiss law (art. 340 CO: clause de non-concurrence is only valid if limited to place, time and subject matter in a way that's necessary to protect legitimate business interests — typically max 3 years). Should I mention this? The user explicitly said "Ne change aucune formulation, ne reformule rien" — so I must not change the wording. But I can add a brief note outside the corrections that this clause may be legally problematic. That would be genuinely helpful for a small business owner hiring their first employee. However, I should be careful not to overstep — the user asked only for spelling corrections. A brief note is helpful and doesn't violate the instruction since I'm not changing the text. I think a short remark is appropriate and valuable — the clause as written (5 years, entire Switzerland, any sector) would almost certainly be null under art. 340 al. 1 CO. Also, employees under a certain wage threshold (below CHF 120,000/year? Actually art. 340a CO: non-compete clauses are not binding on employees with a monthly salary exceeding CHF 10,000... no wait, it's the opposite: the prohibition applies to employees whose annual salary does not exceed CHF 120,000? Let me recall: Art. 340a CO: "La clause de non-concurrence n'est pas contraignante pour les travailleurs dont le salaire annuel ne dépasse pas 120'000 francs." Hmm, actually I need to recall correctly: Art. 340a al. 1 CO: The non-compete clause is not binding for workers whose annual wage does not exceed 120,000 francs? Let me think. The provision: "La clause d'interdiction de concurrence n'est pas obligatoire pour les travailleurs dont le salaire annuel brut ne dépasse pas 120'000 francs." Wait, no — I think it's the reverse: it's NOT binding for workers whose annual salary does NOT exceed CHF 120,000. So an employee earning 5'200/month = 62'400/year would be under 120'000, meaning the clause is not binding anyway. Yes, art. 340a al. 1 CO: "La clause d'interdiction de concurrence n'est pas contraignante pour les travailleurs dont le salaire annuel ne dépasse pas 120 000 francs." So for this employee at 62,400/year, the clause is not binding at all. That's very relevant info for the employer. But should I include it? The user asked only for orthography. I'll add a brief note after the corrected text, clearly separated, mentioning that beyond spelling, this clause appears problematic under art. 340 CO (limitation to place/time/matter necessary to protect legitimate interests; maximum 3 years per jurisprudence) and that they might want to consult a lawyer. Keep it concise. Actually the user is in Lausanne, French-speaking Switzerland — the note in French is appropriate since they wrote in French.

Hmm, but do I risk being annoying? The instruction was very specific. I'll provide the corrections exactly as asked, then a brief "À noter" paragraph. I think that's the right balance — being genuinely helpful. The clause as written would be null and could even expose the employer to liability under art. 340f CO (compensation). A one-liner note is fine.

Let me also double-check Article 4: "L'employé s'engage à travailler 42 heures par semaine, réparties du lundi au vendredi." — spelling fine. Punctuation fine. Note: 42 hours/week exceeds the Swiss legal maximum of 45h (for most workers) — actually 42 hours is fine (legal max is 45h/week in industry/offices, 50h for other workers). No issue there.

Article 7: "Le salaire mensuel brut est de 5'200 francs, verser le dernier jour du mois." — correction: "versé". Keep the comma. Swiss thousand separator with apostrophe is fine (in Switzerland, the apostrophe ' is the official thousands separator per DIN/ISO; commonly written 5'200). Keep as is.

Article 9 corrections:
- "concurent" → "concurrent"
- "concurante" → "concurrente"
- Check "s'interdit": fine.
- "n'importe quel secteur d'activité": fine.
- Punctuation: commas are okay. Actually, one could argue "s'interdit, pendant cinq ans et sur tout le territoire suisse, de travailler..." but the user said don't reformulate. The existing commas: "l'employé s'interdit pendant cinq ans, sur tout le territoire suisse et dans n'importe quel secteur d'activité, de travailler pour un concurrent ou de créer une entreprise concurrente." The comma after "cinq ans" is a bit unusual but not an error per se (setting off the incise "sur tout le territoire suisse et dans n'importe quel secteur d'activité"). Leave punctuation as is — only spelling fixes here. Hmm, is the comma after "cinq ans" correct? The incise is "sur tout le territoire... activité" which is properly enclosed by commas. The first comma after "cinq ans" opens the incise. That's acceptable. Keep.

Article 10: "Le présent contrat est soumi au droit suisse." — "soumi" → "soumis". ("soumis" with -s.) "droit suisse" — adjective, lowercase, correct.

Also "L'employé" — capital after article title period. The format "Article 4 – Durée du travail. L'employé..." — fine.

So the corrections:
1. Article 4: no changes.
2. Article 7: "verser" → "versé".
3. Article 9: "concurent" → "concurrent"; "concurante" → "concurrente".
4. Article 10: "soumi" → "soumis".

I should present the corrected text, and perhaps list the corrections made. The user wants corrected text; showing the corrections list helps them verify. Keep it clean.

Format: Provide corrected text (each article on its own line, as in the original), then a short bullet list of corrections, then optionally a brief note on the non-compete clause. Use French. Keep it concise. Maybe use a small header or just present the text. Since they'll likely copy-paste, present the corrected extracts as a block. I could bold the changes? Bolding inside the contract text might be annoying for copy-paste, but it helps them see. Better: present clean corrected text, then list the corrections below. Yes.

Note on the non-compete: brief. "Au passage, sans toucher à votre texte : une clause de non-concurrence de 5 ans, valable dans toute la Suisse et tous secteurs confondus, a peu de chances d'être valable (art. 340 CO : elle doit être limitée dans le lieu, le temps et l'objet, et ne pas dépasser 3 ans selon la jurisprudence). Par ailleurs, art. 340a CO : elle n'est pas contraignante pour un salaire annuel ≤ 120'000 francs. Un juriste pourrait vous aider à l'ajuster." — Keep to 2-3 sentences. Since the employee earns 5'200/month (62'400/year), the clause isn't binding at all. That's important. I'll mention both points briefly.

Actually, let me double check art. 340a CO: "1 La clause d'interdiction de concurrence n'est pas contraignante pour les travailleurs dont le salaire annuel ne dépasse pas 120 000 francs." Yes, that's correct. So for this salary, the clause is not binding on the employee. Good to flag.

And art. 340 al. 1: clause valid only if "limités dans le lieu, le temps et l'objet de manière à ne pas porter injustement atteinte à l'existence économique du travailleur" and justified by "intérêts dignes de protection du procurant" — and jurisprudence: max 3 years. A clause covering "tout le territoire suisse et n'importe quel secteur" with 5 years is excessive → nulle (in whole or in part, per case law it can be null entirely if excessive). Brief note suffices.

Length: keep moderate. Use markdown lightly: maybe bold "Article" headers? The user gave them inline. I'll reproduce each article as its own paragraph, matching their structure. Then "Corrections apportées :" with bullets. Then "Remarque (hors orthographe)" — short.
